question: The first chairman of the Planning Commission in India was ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India and served from 1947 to 1964.
 
• He was a central figure in Indian politics both before and after independence.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Planning Commission in 1950.
 
• The Planning Commission was formed with the goal of promoting a rapid rise in the standard of living of the people by efficient exploitation of the resources of the country, increasing production, and offering opportunities to all for employment in the service of the community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission of India**

 
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.
 
• It was established on 15 March 1950, and its first chairman was Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The Planning Commission was tasked with assessing the material, capital, and human resources of the country, formulating plans for the most effective and balanced utilization of resources, and determining priorities.
 
• The Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) on 1 January 2015 by the Narendra Modi government, with the aim to better serve the needs and aspirations of the people of India.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**
 
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was an Indian independence activist and the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• He was an important leader of the Indian National Congress and a pivotal figure in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He implemented policies of industrialization and modernization, which laid the foundation for India's future development.
 
• Nehru's vision for India was a secular, socialist, and democratic republic, which he pursued through various reforms and initiatives during his tenure.
